instructions.question: What sentiment does the author of this German tweet express: positive, neutral or negative?
instructions.rule: Judge the author's own expressed feeling, not the topic. Plain news, including factual reports of deaths, accidents, illness or crime, ads, results, fan requests and calm opinions are neutral; headlines are negative only with alarm wording or a quoted victim's grief, and pointed criticism of named politicians or parties is negative. Laughing, winking or heart cues make jokes, teasing, mild gripes and excited surprise positive, but do not soften stated pain or refusal. Bewilderment (o_O, wut, ?!?!), dry sarcasm ('Danke.', 'Aha!'), curt rejections, threats and the author's bad state are negative.

neutral.what: Plain news (also deaths, accidents, illness), sports results, ads, questions, likes, fan requests, calm opinions, mild everyday remarks and absurd jokes.
examples: Selbstmord: US-Schauspieler Lee Thompson Young ist tot - Kultur | STERN.DE Mobile http (Suicide: US actor Lee Thompson Young is dead)
Müdigkeit frisst Motivation #montag (tiredness eats motivation #monday)
Guten Morgen! Wir wollen euch noch erzählen, was #Apple gestern in Sachen #iPhone erzählt hat: http (Good morning! We want to tell you what Apple said yesterday about the iPhone)
neutral.cues: headline plus link, RT of news, prices, Verkaufe (selling), +1, bitte spielt (please play), open questions
neutral.not_for: Headlines with alarm wording, e.g. 'Alarmierende Studie' (alarming study), or a victim's grief are negative. Bewildered o_O reactions are negative.

positive.what: Joy, praise, thanks, stand-alone greetings, welcomes, affection, excitement, pride in success, and jokes or teasing with laughing, winking or heart emoticons.
examples: SIEG!!!!!!!! Chemie gewinnt 2-0 gegen Osnabrück :-D #liga3 (VICTORY!!! Chemie wins 2-0 against Osnabrück)
So unfassbar müde - gute Nacht, ihr Hübschen <3 (so incredibly tired - good night, you lovely people <3)
Schäm dich einfach :P (just be ashamed of yourself :P)
positive.cues: :) / ;) / :D / :P / xD / haha / <3, Gruß (regards), willkommen (welcome), Glückwunsch (congratulations), danke (thanks)
positive.not_for: A smiley after heartbreak or refusal, e.g. 'Herz wieder in tausend Stücke zerfallen. Danke. (:' (heart shattered again. Thanks. (:), is negative. Ads and reported wins are neutral.

negative.what: Complaints, anger, sadness, insults, threats, dry sarcasm, bewilderment, curt rejections, pointed political criticism, the author's bad state, and alarm-worded news.
examples: Och ne, jetzt singt Nicole auch noch? HILFE. #sg (Oh no, now Nicole is singing too? HELP.)
Einmal Weltuntergang zum Mitnehmen bitten. Danke. (One apocalypse to go, please. Thanks.)
Welches Geschenk hast du zuletzt bekommen? — Eine Bettdecke o.O http (What gift did you get last? — A duvet o.O)
RT @user: Alarmierende Studie: 68 Prozent aller Erstwähler können keinen Stift mehr bedienen ... http (Alarming study: 68 percent of first-time voters can no longer use a pen)
negative.cues: :( / :/ / o_O / T_T / wut, scheiße (shit), nervig (annoying), Mist (damn), merkwürdig (weird), einsam (lonely), Aha!, pssst, worst case
negative.not_for: Plain reports or third-party criticism, e.g. 'Forrester-Analyst übt scharfe Kritik' (analyst sharply criticizes), stay neutral. Teasing with ;) and excited 'WTF O.O' are positive.
